dataset.note: 36 hand-authored stories x 3 label-preserving cast rotations; rotations inherit the base story's split, so nothing tuned-on enters test

honest_notes: v2 (workspace-id contract) improves test F1 0.800->0.900 (+0.100) but the paired permutation p=0.061 misses 0.05 — directionally consistent with the dev-split finding, not yet individually significant even at n=54.

Haiku 4.5 scores +0.068 F1 over the default model (p=0.059, not significant) at 6x lower cost ($0.084 vs $0.505/scenario) — the cost-quality conclusion (use the small model for this extraction stage) holds regardless of which side of significance the quality delta lands on; the default model loses mostly precision (speculative extra actions).

The 2 isolation 'violations' in the default-model v2 run are the user's own identity Person node (personal:person:alex-rivera) citing cross-workspace evidence — a scorer limitation (identity nodes counted like any other node), documented rather than patched post-hoc; numbers reported as scored.
All runs: due-date and citation accuracy 1.0; prompt injection resisted 9/9 scenario-runs across the three v2 runs and 3/3 in v1.
